goal: Give the one stable UOR-JCS-NFC refusal code, or admission to the digest, for a JSON document's findings, so every implementation refuses one malformed input with one code.

app.name: jcs-nfc-admission
app.title: JCS NFC admission
app.purpose: Give the UOR-JCS-NFC answer for one document from what admission and canonicalization find in it: the first refusal code by the section 3.9 precedence and the NFC collision check, or addressed when it receives its sha256 digest.

fields.name: bom
fields.means: whether the bytes start with EF BB BF

fields.name: utf8
fields.means: whether the bytes are well-formed UTF-8, raw surrogates included as invalid

fields.name: parse
fields.means: the first parse-time finding in input order, then trailing content after the top-level value

fields.name: names
fields.means: member names: distinct, duplicate after escape decoding, or distinct but colliding after NFC

fields.name: surrogate
fields.means: whether an escaped unpaired surrogate is reached

meanings.addressed: admitted, canonicalized and digested as sha256:<hex>
meanings.e-num-range: E_NUM_RANGE, integer outside plus or minus 9007199254740991
meanings.e-constant: E_CONSTANT, NaN, Infinity or another non-standard constant
meanings.e-trailing: E_TRAILING, content after the top-level value
meanings.e-nfc-collision: E_NFC_COLLISION, member names collide after NFC, never merged

rules.why: SPEC.md 3.2 and 3.9: E_BOM is a byte-level check before parsing and comes first
SPEC.md 3.9: parse-time codes fire in input order
SPEC.md 3.5: tokens such as 1.0 and 1e0 are refused as text
SPEC.md 3.5: values outside the safe-integer bound are refused
SPEC.md 3.6: NaN and Infinity are refused
SPEC.md 3.3 and 3.9: the remainder check follows the parse-time codes
SPEC.md 3.4 and 3.9: duplicates after escape decoding, a post-parse scan
SPEC.md 4.1 and 4.3: NFC precedes member sort, and post-normalization collisions are refused in canonicalization, after admission

app.otherwiseWhy: SPEC.md 5 and uor_jcs_nfc_ref.py address_json: an admitted, canonicalized document is digested

properties.why: one malformed input receives one code, and E_BOM has precedence
a collision is never resolved by last-write-wins, first-write-wins or merging
an integral value such as 1.0 is still refused
a lone escaped surrogate is never digested

stakeholders.name: Context implementer
stakeholders.text: Writes an implementation of the digest context and needs the same refusal code as every other implementation for every input.

stakeholders.name: Registry maintainer
stakeholders.text: Cites the context's final corpus in a registry entry and needs no inadmissible document to receive an address.

components.name: Reference implementation
components.text: uor_jcs_nfc_ref.py, admit and canonicalize written from SPEC.md.

threats.name: Merged colliding names
threats.text: An implementation merges members whose names collide after NFC, giving two documents one address.

control.name: Collision refusal
control.text: Colliding names are refused, never addressed.

threats.name: Integral float admitted
threats.text: A type-based guard admits 1.0 or 2^53 as a float with an integral value.

control.name: Lexical number admission
control.text: Number tokens are validated as text.

threats.name: Different Unicode database
threats.text: NFC under a Unicode version other than 15.0.0 normalizes differently and yields another digest.
threats.accepted: The app takes the collision finding as given; SPEC.md 1.3 pins Unicode 15.0.0, and gen_vectors.py refuses any other runtime.

quality.text: Every malformed combination receives exactly one of the ten refusal codes SPEC.md 3.8 and 4.3 define.
quality.measureText: Distinct refusal codes the app answers.

quality.text: No document with any refusal finding receives an address.
quality.measureText: Acceptance vectors with a refusal finding answered addressed.
